 :Judgment:

This Claim Petition is filed by the Petitioner against the Respondents under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act seeking Compensation of Rs.6,00,000/ for the damages caused to the Mahindra Verito Car bearing Reg.No.KA41A0806 in the Road Traffic accident.

The substance of averments made in the Petition is as under:
The Petitioner is the LR of deceased RC owner of the Mahindra Verito Car bearing Reg.No.KA41A0806.

That on 01.01.2017 at about 7.05 a.m., when the driver of the Mahindra Verito Car bearing Reg.No.KA41A0806 was driving the vehicle from Bengaluru - Bellary road to Airport and reached opposite to Canadian School road, near Venkatala B.B. Road, Yelahanka, Bengaluru, at that time, one Maruthi Swift Vxi Car bearing Reg.No.KA01MJ8106 came from opposite direction in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the CC Camera pole situated at the center of the road and thereafter dashed to the Mahindra Verito Car bearing Reg.No.KA41A0806 and caused accident.
Due to the impact, Mahindra Verito Car was totally damaged.
The accident had occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle.
For repairing the said vehicle, the Petitioner has spent totally sum SCCH 15 4 MVC No.958/2019 of Rs.4,79,414/.

During the period of repair, the Petitioner also spent a sum of Rs.25,000/ towards conveyance charges and she also spent amount towards other incidental charges and she also lost income during the said period.

The said accident is occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the offending Maruthi Swift Car bearing Reg.No.KA01MJ8106 by its driver and the Respondent No.1 being the RC owner and the Respondent No. 2 being the insurer of the Maruthi swift car are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the Petitioner.
3. In pursuance of service of Notice to the Respondents, the Respondent No.1 remained absent and he was placed exparte.
The Respondent No.2 had appeared before the Court through its Counsel and filed its Objection statement to the main Petition.

Vasantha.N vs B.Kumaravelan on 16 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/150736827/
2
In the Objection Statement it has denied the issuance of any policy in favour of the 1st Respondent in respect of Maruthi SCCH 15 5 MVC No.958/2019 Swift Car bearing Reg.No.KA01MJ8106.
Further it denied the accident occurred as the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending car and damage caused to the Verito Car and expenses incurred for the repair of the said car.
Further it contended that none of the drivers holding a valid and effective driving license at the time of accident.
Further it contended that, Verito car is covered by insurance and the insurer has already settled their OD claim with their insurer.
Hence, it is not liable to pay compensation to the Petitioner.
On these grounds, the Respondent No.2 has prayed to dismiss the Petition against it.
4. On the rival Pleadings, this Tribunal has framed the following Issues:

ISSUES 1. Whether the Petitioner proves that the Mahindra Verito Car bearing Reg.No.KA 41A0806 got damaged in a Road Traffic Accident that occurred on 01.01.2017 at SCCH 15 6 MVC No.958/2019 about 7.05 a.m., opposite Canadian School road, near Venkatala, B.B. Road, Yelahanka, Bengaluru, due to the rash and negligent driving of the Maruthi Swift VXI Car bearing Reg.No.KA01MJ8106 by its driver ?
2.
Whether the Petitioner is entitled for the compensation as prayed for?
If yes, what is the quantum and who is liable to pay ?

3 . What Order or Award?
5.
In order to substantiate the case of the Petitioner, the Petitioner got examined her GPA holder as P.W.1 and got marked 16 documents at Ex.P.1 to P.16 and closed her side evidence.
On the other hand, the Respondent No.2 got examined its Administrative Officer as RW.1 and got marked 2 documents at Ex.R1 and 2 and closed its evidence.

6. I have heard the arguments of the learned Counsel for the Petitioner and the learned Counsel for the Respondents and perused the depositions, documents exhibited and SCCH 15 7 MVC No.958/2019 materials available on record.

7. My answer to the above Issues are as under:
 Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative  Issue No. 2 : In the Negative  Issue No. 3 : As per the Final Order  for the following :
 REASONS 8. Issue No.1 and 2: Both these Issues are taken together for common discussion as they are interlinked with each other and to avoid repetition of facts.

Vasantha.N vs B.Kumaravelan on 16 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/150736827/
3

It is the case of the Petitioner that she is the legal heir of deceased Nagaraju who was the RC owner of Mahindra Verito Car bearing Reg.No.KA41A0806 and it got damaged in the Motor Vehicle accident that occurred on 01.01.2017 at about 7.05 a.m.,
9.
On the other hand, the Respondent No.2 has denied the accident caused by the rash and negligent driving of the SCCH 15 8 MVC No.958/2019 driver of the offending Maruthi Swift car.
10. In order to prove the case of the Petitioner, she got examined her GPA holder by name Kumar G.P as P.W.1 and got marked 16 documents at Ex.P1 to Ex.P16.
P.W.1 has re iterated the Petition averments in his chiefaffidavit.
Ex.P1 is the GPA.
Ex.P2 is the Certified copy of FIR, Ex.P3 is the Complaint, Ex.P.4 is the copy of Charge sheet, Ex.P5 is the Spot mahazar with Sketch, Ex.P6 is the IMV report, Ex.P7 is the Service quotation.
Ex.P8 to 11 are the RC, Permit, FC and DL.

Ex.P12 to 16 are the Photos and CD.
11.
Upon going through the Ex.P1, it is the General Power of Attorney executed by the Petitioner in favour of the G.P. Kumar.

Ex.P2 & 3 are the FIR and Complaint, which shows that on the Complaint lodged by one Manjunatha A.N S/o Narayanappa before Yelahanka Traffic Police Station,
the PSI of the concerned Police Station has registered the case against the driver of Maruthi Swift VXi bearing Reg.No.KA01 SCCH 15 9 MVC No.958/2019 MJ8106 for the offences punishable under Sec.279, 337 and 304(A) of IPC.

Ex.P4 is the True copy of the Charge Sheet which shows that after thorough investigation, the PSI of Yelahanka Traffic Police Station has submitted Charge sheet against the driver of the offending Maruthi Swift car for the offences punishable under Sec.
279, 337, 338, 304(A), 427 of IPC and U/s 146 r/w Sec.196 of IMV Act.
12.

Upon going through the Chargesheet i.e., Ex.P4 Column No.7 reads as under :
" 01.01.2017    7.05
SCCH 15 10 MVC No.958/2019

." 
Vasantha.N vs B.Kumaravelan on 16 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/150736827/
4 13.
Ex.P5 is the Spot panchanama along with Sketch which shows that the concerned police had drawn mahazar at the spot in the presence of panchas.
Ex.P6 is the IMV report which shows that the accident does not occurred due to any mechanical defects of the vehicle.
Further IMV report shows the following damages on the vehicle of the Petitioner.
Front bonnet cover, Bumper, both front Head light and indicator damaged 2. Front wind screen glass damaged 3. Left side body damaged 4. Cooling system damaged.
Ex.P.5 is the Service Quotation issued by Sireesh Auto (Pvt.) Ltd., Ex.P8 to 11 are the RC, Permit, FC and DL.
Ex.P12 to 16 are the Photos and CD.
14. PW.1 has subjected for crossexamination by the Learned Counsel for the Respondent No.2.

But,
nothing could be elicited to disbelieve the version of the PW.1 in respect of the accident caused by the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the Swift car bearing Reg.No.KA01MJ8106.

Further IMV report shows that in the said accident of the Verito Car bearing Reg.No.KA41A 0806 got damaged.
15.

The Petitioner is claiming to be RC owner of the Verito SCCH 15 12 MVC No.958/2019 Car bearing Reg.No.KA41A0806 has not produced any document to show that, after the death of her husband, RC of the said vehicle was transferred to her name.
On the other hand, she has also produced RC which marked at Ex.P8 which shows that the RC still stands in the name of Nagaraju.
Ex.P9 and 10 are the Permit and FC it also stands in the name of Nagaraju.
The Petitioner has not produced Death Certificate of her husband to show when her husband / RC owner of the Verito Car bearing Reg.No.KA41A0806 was died.
But, in the Written Arguments submitted by the Learned Counsel for the Respondent No.2, he has mentioned that, the husband of the Petitioner was died on 13.04.2013.
The alleged accident was occurred on 01.01.2017.
It shows that there was 4 years lapsed after the death of Nagaraju / RC owner.
But, the said RC and other documents of the said vehicle still stands in the name of deceased Nagaraju and it is not transferred in the name of the Petitioner.
There is no dispute about the accident caused by the Swift Car bearing Reg.No.KA01MJ 8106.
The RC of the present Verito Car still in the name of deceased Nagaraju.

Though, RW.1 who is the Administrative Officer of the Respondent No.2 Company by name Ramesh P., has admitted in Vasantha.N vs B.Kumaravelan on 16 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/150736827/
5

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: the crossexamination that the said car was attached to the KSTDC, RW.1 shows his ignorance about the suggestion that said Nagaraju was the owner when the car was attached to the KSTDC.

It is to be noted here that though the suggestion putforth to the RW.1 by the Learned Counsel for the Petitioner, he has not produced document to show that at the time of attachment of said vehicle to the KSTDC, the Nagaraju was the owner.
The said Nagaraju was died in the year 2013.
Further, in the crossexamination of PW.1 he answered to the suggestion that, since the Nagaraju was died in the year 2013, the wife of the deceased Nagaraju has filed the present petition.
Further, PW.1 admitted that he has not produced Survey Report and he has not in a position to examine the person, who has issued SCCH 15 14 MVC No.958/2019 Ex.P7 i.e., Service Quotation.
Further he admitted that Ex.P7 is in the document of payment made towards the Service Quotation.
Further he admitted that he is not in a position to produce the Payment receipt which was paid to the garage for the repairs.
Further he deposed that he is not in a position to examine the owner or mechanic of the work shop before this Court.
Further he deposed that the said car is not in a moving stage.

17. The Learned Counsel for the Respondent No.2 has relied on the decision reported in ILR 2000 KAR 2009 in between Karnataka State Road Transport Corporation Vs George Ninum, wherein the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka has pleased held as under:
"Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (Central Act No.59 of 1988) - Section 168 - Claim petition of a person claiming to be the owner of the car, for compensation for repair of the car was allowed rejecting the contention of the KSRTC that claimant's ownership of the car and Special Damages are not proved - Held - in the absence of any material to show that the claimant was the owner of the car, the claim petition itself was not maintainable - Mre producing of documents is not SCCH 15 15 MVC No.958/2019 sufficient to prove Special Damages.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (Central Act No.59 of 1988) - Section 168
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: Such documents have be proved.
Mere production of document is not a proof of its contents."
18. In the instant case also at the time of accident, the Petitioner is not the RC owner of the car.
Further, till today all the documents i.e., RC, Permit, FC, Policy of the said document stands in the name of deceased Nagaraju.
Further, PW.1 admitted that the said Nagaraju was died in the year 2013.
But, the accident occurred in the year 2017.
Though, there is a lapse of 4 years after the death of Nagaraju, the RC and other documents did not get transferred to the name of the Petitioner.
Moreover, the Survey Report has not been produced and the owner or the mechanic of the said garage has not been examined.

Further, PW.1 admitted that, Ex.P7 is only the Service Quotation and not the Payment receipt and he is not in a position to furnish the Payment receipt in respect of the payment made to the garage owner for the repairs.
Under these circumstances, this Tribunal is of the opinion that the Petitioner SCCH 15 16 MVC No.958/2019 is not entitled any compensation.
However, the accident is not in dispute.

Accordingly, I answer Issue No.1 is in the "Affirmative" and Issue No.2 is in the "Negative".
19. Issue No.3:

In view of my findings on Issues No.1 and 2, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The Claim Petition filed by the Petitioner against the Respondent No.1 and 2 U/S 166 of M.V. Act is hereby dismissed with costs.
